context: The input is an ordinary binary tree with 7 nodes. Root 1 has left child 2 and right child 3. Node 2 has left child 4 and right child 5, and 3 has left child 6 and right child 7. Nodes 4, 5, 6, and 7 are leaves.

Preorder follows “root → left subtree → right subtree.” Record each non-null node's value immediately on entry, then recursively process its left and right subtrees in order. Return immediately at a null node.
description: The call path consists of the active recursive calls from the root to the current node. The 11 steps below omit calls on null nodes: 7 steps enter a node for the first time and 4 show upward returns. Steps 4 and 9 return from a left leaf to its parent before moving to the right subtree. Steps 6 and 11 each return two levels in succession.

frames.explanation: Start at root 1 and record 1. The call path is 1 and the output is [1]. Both the left subtree (2, 4, 5) and the right subtree (3, 6, 7) are unvisited. Next, enter left child 2.
frames.title: Visit root 1

frames.announcement: Visit left child 2. The output becomes [1, 2].
frames.explanation: From 1, enter left child 2 and record 2. The call path is 1 → 2 and the output is [1, 2]. Its left and right leaves, 4 and 5, and the root's right subtree (3, 6, 7) are unvisited. Next, enter 4.
frames.title: Visit left child 2

frames.explanation: From 2, enter left leaf 4 and record 4. The call path is 1 → 2 → 4 and the output is [1, 2, 4]. Calls on the empty left and right subtrees of 4 return immediately, after which control will return to 2. Node 5 and the root's right subtree (3, 6, 7) are still unvisited.
frames.title: Visit leaf 4

frames.announcement: Return from leaf 4 to parent 2. The output stays [1, 2, 4]. Next, visit node 2's right child, 5.
frames.explanation: Leaf 4 is complete. Return to parent 2, bringing the call path back to 1 → 2. Returning does not record a node again, so the output stays [1, 2, 4]. The left subtree of 2 is complete. Next, enter right child 5. The root's right subtree (3, 6, 7) remains unvisited.
frames.key_state: Call path: 1 → 2. Output: [1, 2, 4]. Next, visit node 2's right child, 5.
frames.title: Return from 4 to 2

frames.explanation: From 2, enter right leaf 5 and record 5. The call path is 1 → 2 → 5 and the output is [1, 2, 4, 5]. The root's entire left subtree has now been visited, but calls still need to return. Calls on the empty left and right subtrees of 5 return immediately. The root's right subtree (3, 6, 7) remains unvisited.
frames.title: Visit leaf 5

frames.announcement: Return from leaf 5 through 2 to root 1. The output stays [1, 2, 4, 5]. Next, visit root 1's right child, 3.
frames.explanation: When 5 is complete, return to 2. Both subtrees of 2 are complete, so return again to root 1. The call path is back to 1 and the output stays [1, 2, 4, 5]. The root's left subtree is complete. Next, enter its unvisited right subtree (3, 6, 7), starting at 3.
frames.key_state: Call path: 1. Output: [1, 2, 4, 5]. Next, visit root 1's right child, 3.
frames.title: Return from 5 to 1 via 2

frames.announcement: Visit right child 3. The output becomes [1, 2, 4, 5, 3].
frames.explanation: From root 1, enter right child 3 and record 3. The call path is 1 → 3 and the output is [1, 2, 4, 5, 3]. Node 3's left and right leaves, 6 and 7, remain unvisited. Next, enter 6.
frames.title: Visit right child 3

frames.explanation: From 3, enter left leaf 6 and record 6. The call path is 1 → 3 → 6 and the output is [1, 2, 4, 5, 3, 6]. Calls on the empty left and right subtrees of 6 return immediately, after which control will return to 3. Only right leaf 7 remains unvisited.
frames.title: Visit leaf 6

frames.announcement: Return from leaf 6 to parent 3. The output stays [1, 2, 4, 5, 3, 6]. Next, visit node 3's right child, 7.
frames.explanation: Leaf 6 is complete. Return to parent 3, bringing the call path back to 1 → 3. The output stays [1, 2, 4, 5, 3, 6]. The left subtree of 3 is complete. Next, enter the unvisited right leaf, 7.
frames.key_state: Call path: 1 → 3. Output: [1, 2, 4, 5, 3, 6]. Next, visit node 3's right child, 7.
frames.title: Return from 6 to 3

frames.announcement: Visit the final leaf, 7, completing the output [1, 2, 4, 5, 3, 6, 7]. Calls still need to return.
frames.explanation: From 3, enter right leaf 7 and record 7. The call path is 1 → 3 → 7. The output is now complete: [1, 2, 4, 5, 3, 6, 7]. The calls at 7, 3, and 1 are still active and must return.
frames.key_state: Call path: 1 → 3 → 7. Output: [1, 2, 4, 5, 3, 6, 7]. All values have been recorded, but calls still need to return.
frames.title: Visit leaf 7

frames.announcement: Complete the returns through 7, 3, and 1 to end the recursion. The output remains [1, 2, 4, 5, 3, 6, 7].
frames.explanation: After the calls on the empty left and right subtrees of 7 finish, return along 7 → 3 → 1 and finish the root call. All subtrees are complete, the call path is empty, and the final output remains [1, 2, 4, 5, 3, 6, 7].
frames.key_state: Call path: empty. Output: [1, 2, 4, 5, 3, 6, 7]. All calls have finished.
frames.title: Return from 7 to 1 via 3 and finish the calls

summary: A preorder traversal of a 7-node binary tree illustrates the difference between visiting a node and returning to its parent.
title: Recursion in preorder traversal
